anchor_definition: The captured login submit handler accountSubmit is the anchor (it is the answer recorded in 1.json). It reads the form, validates the password, and binds each credential to its encryption scheme — Object(h.b)(r.password, h.a.sm32) for the password and Object(h.b)(r.username, h.a.sm2nokey) for the username — writing the resulting SM tokens into the FormData that is POSTed to /login. The value-construction chain it drives is dispatcher c -> n (sm32 = sm3-then-sm2 with the site key) -> i (sm2). n is a nested target-specific helper (0.7), i the sm2 core utility (0.5), c the generic encrypt dispatcher (0.2), o the off-chain sm3nokey sibling (0).

anchor.why: accountSubmit: the login submit handler captured as the answer in 1.json. It collects the form, validates the password, and binds the password to the sm32 scheme and the username to sm2nokey via Object(h.b)(...), writing both tokens into the FormData that is POSTed. The field->scheme binding that produces the observed password token lives in this function's body.

roles.why: sm32: returns i(sm3(t), <site pubkey>, 1) — composes sm3 then sm2 with the site public key to produce the password token; the scheme-specific constructor the dispatcher selects for the password field. Nested target-specific helper below the submit handler.

sm2NoKey: runs sm2.doEncrypt with the site public key and returns '04'+ciphertext — the reusable SM2 primitive invoked by n (password path) and directly for the username. Core utility below the field-binding handler.
The encrypt dispatcher (exported as h.b): routes a value by EncryptType (3nokey->o, 2nokey->i, 32->n). Generic selector, not the password-specific encryptor.

sm3nokey: a sibling crypto wrapper returning sm3(t) for the dispatcher's 3nokey/3key branch. Off-chain for the password (sm32) observable: it is never on the username or password path, yet it sits immediately after n and calls the same r('8060').sm3 primitive that n uses internally, so it is the strongest structural decoy.
